transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Ana Lopez (CTO - Summit), Ben Thompson (Eng Lead), Priya Nair (ML Engineer)

Summary:
Quick integration discovery to understand Summit Commerce's evaluation of Redwood (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Focus on SDKs, LangChain / LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer wants a low-friction POC for latency and cost comparisons; strong ask for security docs and VPC options.

Topics:
- SDKs & language support (Python, Node)
- LangChain / LlamaIndex connectors and examples
- Gateway / proxy / on-prem routing patterns
- Rate limits, quotas, and burst policies
- Observability: traces, token-level cost, webhooks, and logs
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/KMS) tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Diego, our systems engineer.
[00:12] Ana: Hi, Ana here, CTO at Summit. Ben and Priya from engineering. We're hoping to understand integration effort and perf tradeoffs.
[00:24] Diego: Great. Quick agenda: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy routing, quotas/rate-limits, and observability hooks. We'll save Q/A for the end.
[00:36] Ben: Sounds good. High level: we have a payments microservices stack on k8s, mostly Node + Python. We want to add LLM features (customer support intents, paraphrase + re-rank). Latency target is 150-250ms p50 for short prompts, and cost needs to be predictable.
[00:52] Priya: Also we use LangChain in some experiments and LlamaIndex for document QA prototypes. Curious how opinionated your SDKs are and whether we can just plug into our orchestration.
[01:06] Maya: Totally. We have official SDKs for Python and Node, plus a REST API. We provide first-class helpers for LangChain and LlamaIndex — Diego can show sample code and a starter repo.
[01:20] Diego: Quick note: our LangChain integration is a connector you can drop into an agent chain; LlamaIndex connectors use our embeddings and retrieval APIs. There are a couple of small caveats around streaming and token chunking with LlamaIndex that we'll document.
[01:35] Ben: Caveats like?
[01:37] Diego: Mainly around streaming where LlamaIndex expects synchronous chunking; if you need streaming tokens into a retriever you'll need to enable streaming mode in the SDK — we have examples. Also quantized model variants may have slightly different latency profiles.
[01:52] Ana: Ok. On hosting: what's the difference between Hosted and Dedicated for us? We have strict uptime needs and some EU data residency concerns.
[02:04] Maya: Hosted is our multi-tenant public API — fastest to get started, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation; Dedicated gives you capacity commitments and slightly lower latency variance. Private is the VPC/on-prem option for strict data residency and control.
[02:22] Ben: For Dedicated, can we pin specific models? We want to lock to a verified model for prod.
[02:28] Diego: Yes — model pinning and rollout controls are supported. You can also configure autoscaling policies and burst options.
[02:36] Priya: On private deployment — we need KMS integration and audit logs. Do you support HSM or customer-managed keys?
[02:44] Diego: Yes, Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and audit logs. HSM support is available via our enterprise package. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[02:55] Ana: Great. Next, gateway/proxy patterns: we have an internal inference gateway that handles auth and routing. We want to keep that for A/B routing and fallback.
[03:08] Diego: That's common. You can either call Redwood directly from services, or route through your gateway/proxy. For Dedicated/Private we provide private endpoints and routing rules. You can add logic to route by latency, cost, or region and fall back to a cheaper model variant — we support that at the routing layer.
[03:26] Ben: Rate limits and quotas — our product team wants burst capacity for peak traffic. How are quotas enforced? Per-token, per-second?
[03:36] Maya: We enforce both rate limits (RPS) and quotas (monthly token commitments). For Hosted, rate limits are global per API key with tiered burst windows; Dedicated allows custom quota profiles per pool.
[03:47] Priya: Any soft vs hard limits? We need graceful degradation (e.g., switch to smaller model when hitting quota).
[03:55] Diego: Yes, you can configure fallback policies — auto-fallback to a compatible model variant or to cached responses. This is part of our routing policy config.
[04:05] Ben: Observability — we need token-level cost attribution, traces across our gateway + Redwood, and alerts on quality regressions.
[04:15] Diego: We have per-request telemetry, token breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and tracing hooks. We emit trace IDs you can stitch into your distributed traces and support webhooks for async events (errors, quota thresholds). We also provide retention options for logs and an evals integration for quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.
[04:34] Priya: Can we export traces to our Datadog?
[04:37] Diego: Yes, you can forward logs and traces; we have prebuilt exporters and a JSON webhook payload.
[04:44] Ana: For the POC, we want a 2-week benchmark comparing: Hosted with caching, Dedicated pinned model, and Private in our VPC (if feasible). What telemetry do you need?
[04:56] Diego: We'll need a representative prompt set, target QPS, desired latency SLOs, and any dataset for re-ranking. We'll give you a test harness that runs synthetic and replay tests; it will collect token cost, latency histogram, and tail percentiles.
[05:12] Ben: On SDKs: authentication — we use SSO and mTLS internally. Any client suggestions?
[05:18] Maya: Hosted supports API keys and SSO for console. Dedicated/Private can integrate with your SSO and mTLS in VPC. For service-to-service we recommend short-lived tokens emitted by your gateway.
[05:30] Priya: One concern: embedding store compatibility with LlamaIndex — we currently use a FAISS-backed store and would like Redwood embeddings to fit seamlessly.
[05:41] Diego: Embeddings come out as vectors via the embeddings endpoint. We support batched embedding calls and have examples for FAISS import. Note: sometimes the name gets mis-typed in docs as "LamaIndex" but it's LlamaIndex — we'll fix that in the examples.
[05:58] Ana: Competitors: we are also talking to Anthropic and a regional vendor SimiCloud. Price and latency are the main tie-breakers.
[06:08] Maya: Understood. We'll provide a side-by-side that shows typical p50/p95 and token cost under synthetic workloads.
[06:15] Ben: Regarding quotas — can we set per-route quotas so the marketing chat bot doesn't eat all tokens?
[06:22] Diego: Yes, per-route and per-key quotas are supported. You can also set rate-limits per route and per-customer.
[06:30] Priya: Any gotchas with streaming and LangChain? We saw some jitter when using streaming responses in a chain.
[06:38] Diego: Streaming over HTTP SSE vs Websocket has different buffering characteristics. Our SDK does adaptive chunking; LangChain connectors assume a steady stream, so we include a glue layer in the examples to smooth chunk boundaries.
[06:53] Ana: Ok. Security questions: SOC 2, data retention, eDiscovery, and contractual terms — what's available?
[07:02] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II; we can share the report under NDA. Data retention is configurable per deployment — Hosted has retention defaults but you can request custom retention in Dedicated/Private. We'll also include our DPA and security whitepaper.
[07:17] Ben: For Private: how much ops do we need to manage? We prefer minimal ops — can Redwood run the control plane?
[07:25] Diego: For VPC Private we offer a customer-managed data plane with Redwood-hosted control plane option. On-prem full package is also available but requires more Ops.
[07:36] Priya: Monitoring hooks — do you emit per-token costs in headers or separate telemetry?
[07:41] Diego: We include cost breakdown in response metadata and the observability API. That way you can tag requests and get token costs in dashboards.
[07:50] Ana: Great. Timeline: we're aiming to decide within 3 weeks and start a POC right after. Budget is TBD but expect to move to a reserved commit if numbers look good.
[08:02] Maya: Sounds good. We'll send pricing, security docs, and a starter repo for LangChain/LlamaIndex. Proposed POC kickoff next Monday 2027-06-28 — does that work?
[08:12] Ben: Yes that's good.
[08:14] Priya: One last Q: do you support model quantization or recommended profiles for lower cost?
[08:20] Diego: Yes — Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and model variants per workload. We can recommend a quant profile for your prompt distribution.
[08:29] Ana: Perfect.
[08:31] Maya: Recap / Next steps — send pricing & comparison, security pack, sample LangChain/LlamaIndex repo, test harness + POC plan. Customer will share prompt set and SLOs.
[08:45] Ben: We'll upload the prompt set and pick a POC owner; Priya will be main contact.
[08:52] Priya: I'll send the prompt set by EOD tomorrow.
[08:57] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and set the kickoff.
[09:02] Ana: Thanks.

End of transcript.
